processing: A flat, pan-fired green tea made from tender spring buds, pressed straight in the pan to give its sparrow-tongue shape.
harvest_season: Spring, using tender buds picked around Qingming.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight, even buds shaped like a sparrow's tongue, glossy green.
appearance_wet: Tender, even buds and young leaves.
taste_profile: Fresh and brisk, with a lasting chestnut aroma alongside clean, floral and sweet notes.

brewing.notes: General advice for flat green teas: cooler water keeps the chestnut note clean. Pour the water in gently, since flat buds float at first.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring harvest, with lots picked around Qingming the ones to look for. Drink it within the year, as with other green teas.
description:
Jintan Queshe is a flat green tea from Jintan in southern Jiangsu, with the Fanglu tea farm as its best known home. Queshe means sparrow's tongue, a shape name shared by teas in several provinces, so the place is the part of the name that matters.

It uses tender buds from the spring flush, pan-fired flat and straight.

The aroma is lasting and chestnutty, with clean floral and sweet notes around it, and the cup is fresh and brisk. Use water around 80 degrees and do not rush to a very long steep.

The name has national geographical indication status. Look for Jintan on the label and for this year's spring date.

If you like it, try Maoshan Qingfeng, another flat green from the same area.
history: This is a young tea: it was created in the 1980s, in a Jiangsu tea scene that was adding new premium names at the time. Its name comes from its shape, and it has since gained a national geographical indication and regional brand recognition.
